root_help:
Usage: root [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...                                        
                                                                                
 Operate the Personal Health Data Mirror.                                       
                                                                                
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --install-completion          Install completion for the current shell.      │
│ --show-completion             Show completion for the current shell, to copy │
│                               it or customize the installation.              │
│ --help                        Show this message and exit.                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ status                  Show synchronization and backfill status.            │
│ backfill                Start or resume the historical backfill and wait for │
│                         completion.                                          │
│ sync                    Run incremental synchronization for one or every     │
│                         configured data type.                                │
│ reconcile               Re-read a recent window across every mirrored data   │
│                         type.                                                │
│ webhook-readiness       Report secret-safe Google Health subscriber          │
│                         prerequisites.                                       │
│ webhook-status          Show secret-safe local webhook receipt and           │
│                         processing status.                                   │
│ webhook-replay-pending  Retry durable pending webhook elements without       │
│                         asking Google to resend them.                        │
│ verify                  Check archive guards, payload and body hashes,       │
│                         version history, and sync errors.                    │
│ history                 List every stored version of raw records (oldest     │
│                         first) as JSON.                                      │
│ import-versions         Add payload versions (and whole records) that only   │
│                         survive in old dumps.                                │
│ identity-backfill       Decide source chains, add v2 aliases and link        │
│                         duplicate rows of a record (idempotent).             │
│ identity-decide         Decide what the reconciler left open: two sources    │
│                         are one device, or two devices.                      │
│ identity-sources        List a data type's source fingerprints: spans,       │
│                         devices, chains (with review state),                 │
│                         pairs kept apart, the owner's decisions, and what    │
│                         the chain rule leaves open.                          │
│ responses               List stored Google responses (newest first, metadata │
│                         only) as JSON.                                       │
│ export-response         Write one stored Google response body byte for byte  │
│                         (metadata goes to stderr).                           │
│ probe                   Probe accessible Google Health types without         │
│                         archiving records or a backfill.                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

history.help:
Usage: root history [OPTIONS]                                                  
                                                                                
 List every stored version of raw records (oldest first) as JSON.               
                                                                                
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  --data-type                    <str>                 Google data type,    │
│                                                         e.g. heart-rate.     │
│                                                         [required]           │
│    --id                           <str>                 One record's         │
│                                                         google_data_point_id │
│                                                         (shown even with one │
│                                                         version).            │
│    --since                        <%Y-%m-%d|%Y-%m-%dT%  Only records         │
│                                   H:%M:%S>              replaced at or after │
│                                                         this UTC date/time.  │

│                                   [1<=x<=10000]         changed records.     │
│                                                         [default: 20]        │
│    --payload      --no-payload                          Include raw          │
│                                                         payloads.            │
│                                                         [default: payload]   │

│                                                         and exit.            │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

identity-backfill.help:
Usage: root identity-backfill [OPTIONS]                                        
                                                                                
 Decide source chains, add v2 aliases and link duplicate rows of a record       
 (idempotent).                                                                  
                                                                                
 Decides, from the sightings, that two sources are one renamed device (the      
 owner decides                                                                  
 the rest with identity-decide). The report lists, per data type, every chain   
 (from -> to                                                                    
 source, gap in seconds, review state), the chains to review, the sources the   
 rule left                                                                      
 open (``ambiguous``, with why), refuted chains, and the pairs of sources that  
 share a class                                                                  
 but are kept apart; review them after a dry run (docs/RUNBOOK.md).             
                                                                                
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --batch-size               <int range>              [default: 5000]          │
│                            [100<=x<=100000]                                  │
│ --dry-run                                           Report only; write       │
│                                                     nothing.                 │
│ --data-type                <str>                    Only this data type      │
│                                                     (repeatable); default:   │
│                                                     every archived type.     │
│ --after                    <%Y-%m-%d|%Y-%m-%dT%H:%  Only rows starting       │
│                            M:%S>                    at/after this UTC time   │
│                                                     (resume a stopped run of │
│                                                     --data-type).            │
│ --incremental                                       Only rows changed since  │
│                                                     each data type's         │
│                                                     checkpoint (what the     │
│                                                     nightly job runs).       │
│ --statement-timeout        <str>                    PostgreSQL               │
│                                                     statement_timeout for    │
│                                                     each batch (e.g. 120s,   │
│                                                     5min).                   │
│                                                     [default: 120s]          │
│ --help                                              Show this message and    │
│                                                     exit.                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.help: Report only; write nothing.

parameters.name: data_type
parameters.help: Only this data type (repeatable); default: every archived type.

parameters.name: after
parameters.help: Only rows starting at/after this UTC time (resume a stopped run of --data-type).

parameters.name: incremental
parameters.help: Only rows changed since each data type's checkpoint (what the nightly job runs).

parameters.name: statement_timeout
parameters.help: PostgreSQL statement_timeout for each batch (e.g. 120s, 5min).

identity-decide.help:
Usage: root identity-decide [OPTIONS] {decision}                               
                                                                                
 Decide what the reconciler left open: two sources are one device, or two       
 devices.                                                                       
                                                                                
 Recorded append-only (raw_source_decisions) and applied at once; the rows      
 whose devices                                                                  
 change are settled again. ``link`` joins two sources into one device (their    
 rows are                                                                       
 linked where they hold the same reading); ``reject`` stops using a chain: its  
 links no                                                                       
 longer hide anything, both sources count on their own (each record once per    
 device), and                                                                   
 ``confirm`` undoes that; ``confirm`` also takes a chain off the review list;   
 ``distinct``                                                                   
 declares two devices (a row whose reading then comes back only under the other 
 source is                                                                      
 marked deleted by the next complete fetch: permanent) and ``not-distinct``     
 undoes it. Run                                                                 
 with --dry-run first (docs/RUNBOOK.md).                                        
                                                                                
╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    decision      <str>  link, reject or confirm (a chain FROM -> TO);      │
│                           distinct or not-distinct.                          │
│                           [required]                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *  --data-type         <str>                      [required]                 │
│ *  --from              <str>                      Fingerprint (prefix, as    │
│                                                   reports print it) of the   │
│                                                   earlier form.              │
│                                                   [required]                 │
│ *  --to                <str>                      Fingerprint (prefix) of    │
│                                                   the later form.            │
│                                                   [required]                 │
│    --note              <str>                      Why (kept with the         │
│                                                   decision).                 │
│    --dry-run                                      Report the effect; write   │
│                                                   nothing.                   │
│    --batch-size        <int range>                [default: 5000]            │
│                        [100<=x<=100000]                                      │
│    --help                                         Show this message and      │
│                                                   exit.                      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

parameters.name: decision
parameters.help: link, reject or confirm (a chain FROM -> TO); distinct or not-distinct.

parameters.name: first
parameters.help: Fingerprint (prefix, as reports print it) of the earlier form.

parameters.name: second
parameters.help: Fingerprint (prefix) of the later form.

parameters.name: note
parameters.help: Why (kept with the decision).

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.help: Report the effect; write nothing.
